newsitem.title: UK: Buoyant Nigerian crudes helped by eastern sales.
newsitem.headline: Buoyant Nigerian crudes helped by eastern sales.

text.p: Nigerian crude differentials stayed in the stratosphere on Thursday despite lobbying from some crude contract holders ahead of next week's release by NNPC of term prices for November.
Nigerian values were helped by Taiwanese CPC's decision not to opt out of its term contract purchases from Elf for November despite the poor economics dictated by a very wide Brent/Dubai spread.
CPC will take two November VLCCS, shared three parts Forcados one part Angolan Palanca aboard one and three Forcados one Odudu on the second, traders said.
Korean Yukong might also have bought light Nigerian crude for end November loading to feed new refining capacity, traders said. But the purchase could not be confirmed.
Six cargoes of Qua Iboe are already committed to India in its November tender purchase.
Premiums over Brent were established at 70 cents for Bonny Light and Medium in a sale to a Spanish refiner on Wednesday.
Forcados, difficult to pin down in a secretive market, was put nearer to +80 cents.
"No-one wants to admit it because NNPC prices are out next week, but this market's on fire," said one buyer without an NNPC contract.
The only possible dampener on rising premiums was the reversal in U.S. heating oil and European gas oil markets on Wednesday, dealers said.
North Sea physical markets were steady in a market with little left to trade for October.
Brent 15-day spreads shrank in line with weaker outright values. Oct/Nov traded at +40 cents, four cents below offers of +44 heard in the morning. Nov/Dec was done at +65.
